Mowgli came from another zoo and was not purchased as a pet. The reason Mowgli is inside the house (which is on the zoo property) is because he is not fully vaccinated and we will not allow him outside until our vet clears us for that. Anyone who is wanting a pet tiger needs to know that you cannot legally own one as a pet. Also, this is not Rick’s first Tiger. You can go and see Kai, our female, on our page. Rick has extensive experience with big cats and raising them. You can however enjoy how cute he is on our social media! We will NEVER have tiger encounters available and no visitors will ever be allowed to touch him or interact with him. When he is older and cleared to go outside you can see him in his enclosure if you visit the zoo. We hope that clears a few things up!

Why Do Tigers Spray This Strange Liquid? 🐅 When a tiger sprays urine onto a tree, it isn’t just marking territory—it’s leaving behind a chemical message. The scent can reveal information about the tiger and signal to others that the area is already occupied. This powerful form of scent communication helps tigers defend territory, find potential mates, and avoid unnecessary confrontations in the wild.

Grumpy Kallie is waiting for breakfast. 😊 Today, on International Tiger Day, we’re honored to introduce you to Kallie—a tiger whose survival is nothing short of a miracle. When Kallie was rescued by Lions Tigers & Bears, she had been abandoned and left to die. Her condition was so critical that she required extensive emergency medical care, multiple surgeries, and ultimately a life-saving leg amputation. Against all odds, Kallie never gave up. Today, Kallie is thriving on three legs, living the life she always deserved at Lions Tigers & Bears. She continues to receive specialized daily care from our dedicated team, and every step she takes is a reminder of what’s possible when compassion meets action. Your support made Kallie’s second chance possible. Thank you for standing with us as we rescue, rehabilitate, and provide lifelong sanctuary to animals who have nowhere else to turn. Happy International Tiger Day.

Why Tigers Look Invisible to Deer 🐅👀 To us, a tiger’s orange coat looks impossible to miss. But deer see color differently from humans, making those bright orange tones much harder to distinguish from the greens and browns of the forest. That unusual vision may help tigers stay concealed while stalking their prey. 🐅🌿

❗️ 🐅👑💀 Arrowhead: The Queen of the Lake 😱🌅 She wasn't just another tiger in Ranthambore. Arrowhead, also known as T-84, became one of the reserve's most recognizable tigresses—carrying a legendary bloodline and ruling some of the park's most prized territory. 🐅👑 Arrowhead was the daughter of the famous tigress Krishna (T-19) and granddaughter of the legendary Machli. 🌅🌿 Her territory around Ranthambore's lakes, including the area near Padam Talab, made her a favorite among wildlife photographers. 👑🐾 Her powerful presence and long reign helped make her one of the park's most celebrated tigresses. 🧬🐅 Through her lineage, Arrowhead continued one of Ranthambore's best-known tiger family lines. 🌊👁️ The lakes and surrounding forests provided essential habitat for a territorial predator like her. ⏳🖤 In her later years, images showed a visibly aged and weakened tigress—a stark contrast to the powerful hunter she once was. 🌅🐅 Her final chapter became a poignant reminder that even the most dominant predators eventually face age, weakness, and the passage of time. For years, she walked beside the lakes like she owned the wilderness. Then time began taking what strength could not. The Queen of the Lake became a symbol of Ranthambore itself—powerful, wild, famous, and ultimately mortal. 🐅👑💀 Did you ever see Arrowhead during her reign at Ranthambore?❗️#nature #wildlife #animals #tiger #jungle
